text:
support-alice: Hey team - multiple customers reporting 502/504s to the hosted API (/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-14T10:12Z. Lots of noise in helpdesk, CS escalated. Samples attached by customers show upstream 502s and timeouts. :rotating_light:
support-alice: One customer has a replay with curl showing consistent 504 after ~25s. cURL: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

ethan-oncall: I'm on it. Can someone paste the last 10m of Envoy logs and upstream 5xx rate?
maria-sre: Pasting summary from Datadog: `edge.envoy.5xx_rate` spiked from 0.2% -> 6.8% between 10:11-10:18Z. Latency p95 for /v1/generate jumped to 4.2s. Host-level CPU on edge-gw nodes looks normal, but connection errors to auth-service increased.
maria-sre: Log excerpt (Envoy):
```
[10:13:02] envoy access_log: "GET /v1/generate HTTP/2" 504 - upstream_rq_timeout
[10:13:02] envoy upstream: connection failure: "upstream reset" to 10.3.45.12:8443
[10:13:03] envoy tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
```

sanjay-runtime: The `upstream_rq_timeout` suggests Envoy isn't getting responses from the auth-check or runtime proxy. Did we recently roll auth-service or change certs?

liz-pm: No cert roll for auth-service this week. We did push a config change to the runtime routing a canary model yesterday but it was small.

ethan-oncall: Querying Loki for auth-service latency: shows burst of 5xx from auth around 10:10-10:16. Example: `auth.ValidateToken: returned 500, duration=324ms, err=sql: connection refused`

maria-sre: So chain is: client -> edge Envoy -> auth-service -> runtime. If auth returns 5xx, Envoy can convert to 502/504 depending on timing and retry policy. The TLS handshake error might be clients hitting an older cert during a rotated upstream IP.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed auth-service v2.14.8 at 2026-03-14T09:58Z to cluster-us-east.

ethan-oncall: Aha, v2.14.8 had a DB connection pooling change that may underprovision max conns. Looks like auth started hitting DB connection limits under a small spike. That would make it return 500s and cause Envoy upstream resets/timeouts.

support-alice: Customers reporting it affects both generation and embeddings endpoints. Any mitigation we can apply quickly?

maria-sre: Short term mitigations: 1) increase auth-service replicas and scale DB read pool, 2) add Envoy retry policy for transient 5xx with small backoff, 3) temporarily route traffic to auth fallback (stateless verifier) for edge requests > canary flag. I'll action 1 and 2 now.

sanjay-runtime: For the Envoy config, let's avoid infinite retries — do `retry_on: 5xx` with `num_retries: 2` and `per_try_timeout: 2s`. That reduces client-perceived 502 storm without masking hard failures. Also increase `upstream_connection_timeout` to account for cold starts.

ethan-oncall: Scaling auth to +3 pods now. Patching Kubernetes HPA and bumping DB max connections.

maria-sre: Patch applied to edge Envoy config: added retries and per-try timeouts, and raised `idle_timeout` from 30s -> 60s for upstreams that are showing TLS handshake flakiness. Rolling out to us-east edge nodes (canary set).

ingress-bot: canary-rollout: envoy-config v1.47 -> v1.48 rolled to 3/12 edge nodes in us-east at 10:42Z.

ethan-oncall: After scaling auth & envoy changes, 5xx rate reduced to 0.6% within 8 minutes. p95 latency back to ~230ms. Still seeing isolated 504s for long-running streams.

maria-sre: The remaining 504s correlate with requests that stream tokens for >60s. Envoy `upstream_rq_timeout` fired at 60s for those; we need a streaming-friendly timeout on those routes. Suggest setting `timeout: 0s` (no timeout) for streaming endpoints and enforce application-level keepalive.

sanjay-runtime: Agreed. We'll create a specific route config for `/v1/stream` endpoints with no proxy timeout and ensure the runtime keeps sending data to avoid idle close. Also add metrics to alert on `envoy.upstream_rq_timeout` per-route.

liz-pm: CS pinged customers with a note about mitigation and ETA for full resolution. They asked whether this was related to billing header changes last week. Any evidence?

ethan-oncall: Not seeing billing header parsing errors in auth logs. The DB errors were classic `too many connections`. I did find one customer replay where the Authorization header was malformed and got a 401 then a follow-up 502 when the runtime tried to parse it — separate issue.

maria-sre: Action items:
- (ethan) postmortem on auth rollout v2.14.8 and DB pool defaults.
- (sanjay) route-level timeout adjustments for streaming endpoints + Envoy per-route retries config.
- (maria) add alert for `envoy.upstream_rq_timeout` >= 1% over 5m.
- (liz) customer comms and incident blameless summary.

support-alice: Customers updated, most reporting service mostly back. One enterprise tenant still sees occasional 502s; Ethan to take offline to triage with them.

ethan-oncall: I'll open a tenant-level trace and meet with CS. For followups: revert the DB default pool settings on rollout, add a smoke test for auth DB load, and add a rollout guard in deploy pipeline to check DB connection cap.

maria-sre: We'll also document an incident runbook for edge 502/504s that covers auth 5xx as a common root cause and repro commands. Repro snippet for support/devs: `ab -n 200 -c 20 -p payload.json -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` and watch `auth.requests.error_rate`, `edge.envoy.5xx_rate`.

sanjay-runtime: Marking incident as mitigated. Plan for root-cause analysis and follow-up change requests.

ops-bot: incident-status: mitigated -> monitoring.

liz-pm: Thanks everyone. I'll schedule a retro tomorrow and link the notes to this thread.

support-alice: Closing the public escalation, keeping this thread for RCAs and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
